compiled_state.description:
## Symptom
A `preview` route pass, and a legacy `--mode dry-run` pass, perform REMOTE Jira writes during pending-binding recovery. Both modes are documented and reported as no-write.

## Evidence (verified by reading the spine)
- `run_differs.py` guards the recovery call with exactly ONE condition, `if not scoped_ids` (where `scoped_ids = ctx.filter_local_ids or ctx.selection_ids`). There is no `persist` / `no_write` / mode condition on it.
- The client it is handed is the real configured transport: `outbound_diff_client = backend.transport`, and `_load_reconcile_backend()` calls `select_backend(load_config())` unconditionally — there is no dry-run branch that substitutes a no-op transport.
- The keyed-pending branch of `recover_pending_bindings` then calls `client.add_label(key, "rebar-id:<local_id>")` and `client.set_entity_property(key, "local_id", <local_id>)`. Those are mutations of the remote issue.
- For contrast, the sibling invariant-filing gate in the same function DOES compose both axes: `skip_invariant_filing = (not persist) or bool(scoped_ids)`. So the omission on the recovery call is asymmetric with the code beside it.

Net effect: `persist=False` suppresses the local binding-store `save()` (it sits inside `reconcile.py`'s `if persist:` block), so the LOCAL side of recovery is correctly not persisted — but the REMOTE label/entity-property writes still go out. A preview therefore mutates Jira and then throws away the local record of having done so, which is also the least recoverable combination.

## Why this was not fixed in RP-02 S3
RP-02 S3 adds a NEW recovery operation (interrupted-retirement completion) and gates it on `persist and not scoped_ids`. It deliberately does NOT change the pre-existing create-recovery gate: that is a behaviour change to load-bearing anti-duplicate machinery, outside an extraction-plus-addition slice, and S3 T1 carries an explicit acceptance criterion that the create-recovery gate is pinned unchanged. The real behaviour is pinned by test, and the correction is filed here.

## Judgement needed before fixing
This is not a one-line gate addition, because there is a real argument on both sides:
- Suppressing recovery on a preview keeps the promise that preview never mutates.
- Recovery exists to prevent duplicate Jira issues after a crash. A preview that skips it is harmless, but an operator who only ever runs preview would never recover a keyed-pending binding.

The likely correct answer is to suppress the REMOTE writes on a no-write pass while still reporting what recovery WOULD do, matching how the rest of preview behaves. That needs its own plan and its own oracles.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A `preview` pass performs zero remote `add_label` / `set_entity_property` calls from pending-binding recovery.
- [ ] A legacy `--mode dry-run` pass performs zero such remote calls.
- [ ] A live pass's recovery behaviour is unchanged, including the keyed-pending no-search rule and the three-miss plus 3600-second keyless conjunction.
- [ ] The chosen disposition (suppress silently vs. report-what-would-happen) is recorded with its rationale.
- [ ] A regression test drives a no-write pass with a keyed-pending binding and asserts zero remote identity writes.
compiled_state.title: Preview and dry-run passes perform remote Jira writes during pending-binding recovery
